default.label: Cannonade ends between 14:30 and 15:00 (Union fire stopped by order about 14:30)
default.basis_text: the lower bound is Hunt's order to stop the Union fire about 2.30 p. m. (Peyton: the Confederate fire abated at 2.30); the upper bound is the slackening about 3 o'clock (Devereux) or two hours from 1 p. m. (Gibbon, Lee, Cabell).

animation.note: The Union guns stop at 14:30 (Hunt's order) and the enemy's fire dies away by about 15:00 as the infantry come out of the woods. 14:30 is the earliest clock reading of an end; durations from about 13:00 give 14:45 to 15:30. 14:00 has no source. The later readings stay selectable.

default.note: The plan's 14:30 and 15:00 are the two bounds of one window; the plan's 14:00 has no source; Hays and Smyth's 16:30 to 17:00 follow their later start.

weighing.summary: The reports that give the end are of three kinds. A clock reading: Hunt, who ordered the Union fire stopped about 2.30 p. m. and says the enemy soon slackened; Peyton (Confederate) 2.30 abated; Devereux just about 3; Howard 3.30 for his own guns. A duration from about 1 p. m.: Hancock one hour forty-five (14:45), Gibbon two hours, Lee about two hours, Cabell over two hours, Meade over two hours (15:00 or later). And two reports of one division, Hays (4.30) and Smyth (5 p. m.), that start the fire an hour late (about 2) and so end it later. The best writers, the gun commanders and the corps and division commanders at the line, differ by about half an hour on a fire that died away rather than stopped on a minute; nothing in the reports separates 14:30 from 15:00, so the end is the window 14:30 to 15:00 and the class is irreducible. 14:00 has no source.
weighing.who: Hunt commanded the artillery of the army and ordered the Union fire stopped; Hancock, Gibbon, Hays, Smyth and Devereux were on Cemetery Ridge under the fire; Howard on Cemetery Hill; Peyton behind the Confederate guns with Pickett's division; Cabell commanded an artillery battalion in the Confederate line; Lee commanded the army from the ridge opposite; Meade commanded the Union army.
weighing.when: Devereux wrote on 7 Jul 1863, Peyton on 9 Jul, Smyth on 17 Jul, Cabell on 1 Aug, Gibbon on 7 Aug, Hunt on 27 Sep, Meade on 1 Oct 1863; Hancock and Howard in 1863; Lee in January 1864. All within weeks or months and of one class; none is a diary of the afternoon. The Park Service handbook (1954) follows them.
weighing.where: Hunt, riding the line behind the Union batteries, saw the batteries and gave the order; Peyton stood behind the crest of Seminary Ridge with his brigade; Hancock, Gibbon, Hays and Smyth lay under the fire; Hays and Smyth faced the Bliss farm and the left of the Confederate line. Howard was a mile and a half to the north.
weighing.how_knew: Hunt gives the hour of his own order (about 2.30); Peyton and Devereux the hour they noted (2.30; about 3); Hancock, Gibbon, Lee, Cabell and Meade give a duration counted from the start, which makes an end only as exact as the start ('about 1') and the count ('about two hours', 'over two hours').
weighing.clock: The Union writers use the Union clock and the Confederate writers theirs; the reported 20-minute difference between the armies' clocks is not applied. It could account for the gap between Hunt's 2.30 (Union) and Peyton's 2.30 (Confederate) being no gap, and a few minutes of the half hour between 14:30 and 15:00, but not for Hays and Smyth, who are Union writers like Hancock.
weighing.independence: The lower bound rests on two separate writers, Hunt (Union order) and Peyton (Confederate abatement). The upper bound rests on Devereux (a clock reading) and on three durations that count from the same signal at about 1 p. m. (Gibbon, Lee, Cabell), each separately. Meade repeats the duration of his corps commanders. Hays and Smyth are one division. The Park Service handbook follows the reports.

source_panel_text: The cannonade ended between 14:30 and 15:00 on Jul 3: Hunt ordered the Union fire stopped about 2.30 p.m. and said the enemy soon slackened; Peyton has the Confederate fire abating at 2.30, Devereux at about 3, and Gibbon, Lee and Cabell about two hours from 1 p.m. No report gives 14:00. Four other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 14:30 holds as the Union ceasefire and the early bound; it is not the end of the whole cannonade, which the line and the Confederates date about 15:00. The plan's 14:00 has no source; 15:00 is the upper bound.

first_delegated.note: 14:30 documented is not exact: the day is not in Hunt's sentence, the tier is inferred, and 15:00 is a bound of the window rather than a later alternative. Its 16:30 to 17:00 holds as the Hays and Smyth reading, explained by their later start.

what_would_change_it: A report, diary or letter of 3 July that gives the hour the last Union or Confederate gun fired, such as the reports of the Confederate battalions on the Peach Orchard line not in the Official Records (Alexander's, Walton's, Eshleman's battalion journals) or of the Union batteries on Cemetery Ridge (Cushing, Brown, Cowan, Hazard's own journal). A page image that reads a different hour in Hunt, Peyton or Devereux would also change it.
